vocabulary.model: Stage A defines 11 correspondence dimensions plus 4 separate cross-cutting checks (Stage A Sections 8.2 and 8.3).
vocabulary.cross_cutting_checks_representation: Each check is recorded per classified case as a structured note with cited evidence and the correspondence dimensions it limits. vocabulary.comparator_rule: Comparator match: can the authoritative buyer-defined comparator be applied faithfully to the evidence value?

plan_rules.rule: A notice or contract document addressed to Harbor about HNS-2025-01 governs Harbor's contracted pricing. A general list-price or catalog announcement does not by itself establish Harbor's contracted pricing.
Copies of one underlying notice received through different paths are one evidence event.

The plan authorizes no interpretation of approximate, bounded, ranged, or qualitative figures. No tolerance band, rounding assumption, confidence value, fuzzy match, or probabilistic threshold satisfaction is applied; such figures leave the affected dimensions UNRESOLVED.

A later item does not supersede an earlier one merely because it is newer. Supersession requires an authority basis: explicit correction or retraction language, version or revision metadata, contractual amendment hierarchy, effective-date logic, or a source rule in this plan. Without one, the affected dimensions stay UNRESOLVED.

The resolved supplier is the contracting legal entity. A name change preserves it only where authoritative evidence establishes the same contracting entity. A changed contracting entity, a changed supplier, an assigned or transferred agreement, or continuity that cannot be established raises BAEC_REVALIDATION_REQUIRED. Name similarity never establishes continuity.

The plan does not define which price measure (base price, fees, landed cost, single SKU, or spend-weighted) the buyer's 'pricing' refers to. That remains a human finding grounded in the buyer's evidence.
